answer: Count what it costs to copy an identity, then weight that by how far the copy travelled from the original. An agent with three separate histories costs three times as much to fake as one with a single path. A duplicate shows up when the payload is replayed, not when the name is checked. Names are free, payloads are not. A farm pays per copy and again per fabricated path, so the yarrow of aliases it plants yields nothing until each one carries a real history. A raven can imitate one call, not a flock. The haven holds only while the paths stay independent.
